svg.aria-label: Flowchart of HBRIDGE serial commands for the Limiter and ECH-HVPS controllers. Connect and identify, confirm IDLE, optionally recall a saved profile, choose the supply and the phases, check the fault inputs, upload the shot and read it back, ARM, start with FIRE or the PF15 trigger, poll while firing, and return to IDLE. A fault from any state leads to FAULT:SOURces?, finding the input, removing the cause, FAULT:CLEar, and a STATE? check before returning to IDLE. The CHARGE output is separate from the state.
svg.text: Open TCP to the hub: port 5102 Limiter, 5103 ECH-HVPS
OK ARMED or OK FIRING: another session
is using it. Stop and look.
OK FAULT GENERAL: take the fault path.
Optional: start from a saved profile
IDLE only. Then go on from "Read it back": a profile holds
the supply, the phases, the shot and the fault-input settings.
A recall can switch protections off
SPARKOFF count fault inputs now switched off.
It can also change phases and dead time.
NONE after every reset. A change discards the uploaded shot.
The limits the shot is checked against
A phase that is off is never connected to its output pins.
Fault inputs: look before every session
Expect every input on and the bypass 0, unless agreed otherwise.
IDLE or FAULT only. On again at every reset.
An unwired input can read as a fault.
Upload the shot: one line, one reply
First at t = 0, times increasing, at most 500 setpoints and 1 s.
SHOT:STEP <t_us> 0 0 = output off until the next setpoint.
ERR 4 order, format, or a gap rule
ERR 13 no supply chosen, or FIRING
Gap rules: the first setpoint and the last
two are on. Start again from SHOT:BEGin.
with what was meant: this, not the OK replies, is the proof.
ERR 13 not IDLE, or no phase is on
ARM does not look for a shot: FIRE does.
ARM prepares the start, so the output
begins tens of microseconds after FIRE.
A refused PF15 edge gives no reply:
An edge on PF15 starts the shot with no
Poll until the shot is over
A shot lasts its duration_us: 1 s at most.
Abort. Stops the output, back to IDLE.
Expect OK IDLE and no fault. The shot stays loaded: ARM and
FIRE repeat it. Compare the measured waveform with the demand
OK IDLE, the shot ended by itself
The output stops at once: there is no ramp.
One type only: STATE? says OK FAULT GENERAL.
a fault can arrive in any state
Read the source, then the cause
OK PC10= GATEDRV= TABLE= TEST= OVP= FB=
SPARK=1: the spark-gap input read LOW
OVP=1 or FB=1: a closed loop stopped itself
PC10=1: the hardware fault input tripped
TABLE=1: the shot overran inside the controller
A person finds and removes the cause
Do not switch an input off to get going,
unless that is agreed and written down.
Never auto-clear a fault that hit while firing.
Replies OK whether or not it cleared.
After a reset (a !BOOT line) the supply, the
shot and every setting are gone: start again.
Back to IDLE. Settings and the shot stay until a reset. Every shot needs its own ARM.
The charger is separate from the state
0 = off, otherwise 1 to 100000 Hz. Works in
any state and stays on through a fault.
